accuracy.evidence: Checked against NOAA Ocean Service ('How much oxygen comes from the ocean?' ~half; 'What is ocean acidification?' surface pH 8.2 → 8.1, ~30% rise in acidity, ocean absorbs ~30% of emitted CO₂), the Global Carbon Budget (ocean sink ~a quarter of emissions), IPCC AR6 WG1 (pH ~7.7–7.8 by 2100 under very high emissions, shown as 'about 7.8' at 900 ppm), Lester et al. 2009 (fully protected reserves: biomass on average several times higher inside) and FAO on sustainable fishing. The lab's fishing and zone numbers are labelled as simple models; recomputed: 20/yr keeps 100 fish and lands 200, 30/yr empties the stock in year 5, zone run 594 caught / 88 left vs 558 / 22. The adult text notes sea water stays slightly alkaline.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets ideas reported in ocean-literacy research (Guest et al. 2015 children's ocean perceptions; Ocean Literacy Principle 6 framework): more fishing always means more food (step 1 predict 'Yes, there are lots of fish', tag max), a no-fishing zone must cut the catch (step 2 predict 'It drops to zero', m5, tag die), plastic is harmless or animals 'play' with it (step 3 predict, tag play), acidification means saltier water or nothing (step 4 predict, tags salt and nothing), and one action fixes every threat (step 5 predict about clean-ups and CO₂, tag clean, match feedback naming the right threat).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (no flagship lab over 30% similar). 674 Human impact on environments (flagenvimp) counts kinds in a wood, replants trees and keeps litter out of a river; 732 Ocean food chains, 923 Coral Reefs (flagreef) and 563 What is the ocean (flagocean) never model a fish stock. Only this lab has a catch slider with a 10-year stock chart, a five-zone spillover run with a reserve, a CO₂ dial linked to pH and shell thickness, and a threat-to-fix matcher with decoys.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the sustainable catch by trying values (30 crashes, 10 lands too little, 15–20 works), then sees spillover from comparing two runs side by side, so 'protected areas help nearby fishing' is evidence, not assertion. Clearing litter while leaving the shell, crab and seaweed separates plastic from natural material, the dial ties CO₂ to pH and shells, and the final matcher makes each protection answer a specific threat.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions with tempting wrong options that the task disproves: 'Yes, there are lots of fish' for a 30 catch, 'It drops to zero' for the nearby catch, 'Turtles collect plastic', 'It gets saltier' for CO₂, and 'Yes, it fixes everything' for a beach clean-up. The done message reports the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and specific messages: swim and zoo (what an MPA is), max and never (sustainable fishing still catches fish, but only what grows back), hot and play (turtles mistake bags for jellyfish), salt and nothing (CO₂ makes a weak acid), die (fish spill out of the zone), clean and net (clean-ups do not cut CO₂). Wrong lab moves are named too, e.g. 'Leave the crab! It lives here.' and '“Beach clean-up” is not for “CO₂ and acid sea”…'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid paragraphs define sustainable fishing, marine protected area and more acidic in plain words. Canvas labels are short (Catch: 20 a year, No fishing, Bin 3 / 6, Sea pH about 8.1) and every button says what it does.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler and explanation similarity under 12%. Each kid paragraph carries one protection (threats overview; catch limits; MPAs and spillover; plastic and CO₂ with agreements). The adult text gives standards, model rules with the numbers the learner will see, the real-world evidence, and named mistakes with the pH caveat.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for all six steps and finished states (/workspace/shots/oL-all, oD-all, omid-all, omid0b). Fixed the chart axis overlapping the catch label and moved the Years label after the first pass. Zone columns, litter tiles (3 × 3), the dial with three labelled marks, and the 2 × 2 threat boxes all fit at 360 px with wrapped text.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Catch 5 more, Run 10 years, No fishing in zone 3, Pick up: Straw, CO₂ 420 ppm (Today), Put in: Plastic), and the canvas aria-label states the current values and progress after each action.

sources: NGSS 5-ESS3-1; National Curriculum in England Year 4 living things and their habitats (environments can change)
NOAA Ocean Service: What is ocean acidification? / How much oxygen comes from the ocean?
Global Carbon Budget 2023 (Friedlingstein et al.): ocean CO₂ sink about a quarter of emissions
IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 5: projected surface ocean pH under SSP5-8.5
Lester, S. E. et al. (2009) Biological effects within no-take marine reserves, MEPS 384
FAO: The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture (sustainable and overfished stocks)
